clue.text: Disturbance produced by 13 after port and a game of cards

parts.note: Hull is an English port on the Humber estuary
13 across is ABLE-BODIED, and AB stands for an able-bodied seaman
taken as written
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A row breaks out among sailors in a harbour town over a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is the charade's order signal: the 13 piece comes after the port. AB (able-bodied seaman) is the abbreviation that 13's answer suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is an uproar or commotion, a noisy disturbance.

clue.text: Net brimming, we hear, remains sealed

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the words are said aloud and the spelling changes

parts.note: to net is to earn, and brimming means full

explanation.surface: A fishing net overflowing with catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' is a verb here (earn, as in net a profit), not the fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes kept closed inside a funerary vessel amount to a vessel's full measure of remains.

clue.text: Faithful follower — one, say, embraced by sweetheart

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it, so the first pieces go within the sweetheart word

parts.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart
one is the Roman numeral I
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A loyal follower being hugged by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMAN is an old word for a sweetheart that crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal vassal sworn to serve his lord, hence a loyal follower.

clue.text: Conductor in front of bus, plus the person on top

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here taken from bus

parts.note: plus means and
the one in charge is the master

explanation.surface: A bus conductor standing at the front with the driver on the upper deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'bus' suggest a ticket collector; it is a leader of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandmaster leads and directs a brass or military band, as a conductor does.

clue.text: Supply flower-girl with article for interior

indicators.note: for interior means the article is used as the inside of the girl's name

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name that is also a flower
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone provides a florist's assistant with an item for indoor decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb 'provide' but the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithely means nimbly and flexibly, the way a supple body moves.

clue.text: Sporting contest that's never close

definitions.meaning: a tournament any player may enter, such as golf's championship

explanation.surface: A tournament that is always won by a wide margin.
explanation.definitionFit: An open is a competition for all comers, and the adjective means unshut.

clue.text: Unusual sort of parish

definitions.meaning: a church or parish exempt from the jurisdiction of the local bishop

explanation.surface: An odd kind of church district.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar means odd, and as a noun names a parish outside its bishop's control.

clue.text: Job of worker, on paper, to follow leaders?

definitions.text: Job of worker, on paper, to follow leaders?

parts.words: Job of worker, on paper, to follow leaders?
parts.note: to copy is to follow, and the person in charge of a newspaper writes its leaders, the editorials; the newspaper worker who prepares text for print

explanation.surface: Someone on a newspaper whose job is to imitate their bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: This person corrects and prepares written material for publication at a newspaper or publisher.

clue.text: Work around fruit, mostly citrus

indicators.note: around tells us the word for work is turned the other way

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

explanation.surface: Labour carried on around fruit, most of it citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomelo is a large citrus fruit, ancestor of the grapefruit.

clue.text: Medical student given extremely efficient computer link

parts.note: an intern is a junior doctor in training

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of efficient

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor gets a very efficient connection to a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide network that links computers together.

clue.text: Keen to include leaders of judges in contentious legal group

indicators.note: to include means the hungry word takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: keen as in eager, hungry for something

indicators.note: leaders of points to the opening letters of judges, here its first two

explanation.surface: An eager court wants judges in charge of a disputed legal body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes two opening letters here, JU, not just J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury that cannot agree on a verdict is deadlocked, a group in dispute.

clue.text: Fruit that's fleshy when cut

indicators.note: when cut means the last letter is chopped off the word for fleshy

parts.note: plump means fleshy or chubby

explanation.surface: A fruit that turns out juicy when sliced.
explanation.definitionFit: The plum is a stone fruit.

clue.text: Carriage in station to drive away about one

parts.note: a post is a station, as a sentry's post

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for drive away surrounds the one

parts.note: to chase off is to drive away
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A carriage at the station sets off and drives about.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn travelling coach.

clue.text: Fit chap I included in a bloody issue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: included in means the chap and I sit inside the bleeding word

parts.note: to bleed is to issue blood
bod is slang for a chap or person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A healthy man caught up in a bloody affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody issue' reads as a violent quarrel; it means to bleed.
explanation.definitionFit: Able-bodied means physically healthy and strong.

clue.text: Support less sensitive old-fashioned person

parts.note: to back is to support
more numb, so numb-er, less feeling

explanation.surface: Someone backing a fogey who has lost feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as numb plus ER, more numb.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is an old issue of a magazine, so figuratively someone out of date.

clue.text: Be likely to be ready for attack

definitions.meaning: as in ... win, to be in line to gain
the military order for troops to take up positions against an assault

explanation.surface: Probably poised for an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand to means to be in a position to gain, and soldiers stand to before dawn in readiness.

clue.text: European stealing a pound from another continental type

indicators.note: stealing means a letter is taken away from the next word

parts.note: an Australian is a native of another continent

explanation.surface: A European robs a person from another continent of a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' suggests mainland Europe, but here it is Australia, the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian is a native of Austria, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Doomed by an old spell

definitions.meaning: cursed by a spell of long ago, and also the word in an old-fashioned spelling

explanation.surface: Doomed by an ancient enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurst, an archaic spelling of accursed, means under a curse, so doomed.

clue.text: Special ad I've run for uniform

indicators.note: special suggests these letters are specially arranged in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Beat it, producing second grouse

clue.text: I'm able to follow the other lead for native of republic

clue.text: Change of direction that's very short always

parts.note: very in short form is V
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A sudden turn that is always brief.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swerve, a sudden change of course.

clue.text: English author, such as Waugh

definitions.meaning: ... Waugh, the novelist, had this first name

explanation.surface: An English novelist like Evelyn Waugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The diarist John Evelyn bore this surname, and the novelist Waugh bore it as a first name.

clue.text: Eastern city where disorder returns within a month

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: within means the reversed disorder goes inside the month

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March

indicators.note: returns means the word for disorder comes back, read the other way

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or disorder

explanation.walkthrough: Disorder is apt: Amritsar in India saw the 1919 massacre.

clue.text: For example, Southern states

explanation.surface: The southern US states, for instance.

clue.text: Cup Billy contrived to get in 6

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Eponymous hero mixed drink

clue.text: Going on board for sea crossing

to cross a horse is an old phrase for to mount and ride it
